admission.justification: The two governing Architect rulings extend the existing rule6 boundary with requested-fetch permission(d); rule8 requires explicit current decision guidance.

alternatives.option: Keep admitted(a)-(c) and add(d): when the caller of a context read asks for freshness, the writes of one `git fetch` of the configured upstream, all inside the Git directory: the fetched objects, the remote-tracking refs and their reflogs, `FETCH_HEAD`, a tag that Git's fetch follows by its default, and Git's own housekeeping after a fetch. It changes no local branch, no HEAD, no index and no file of a working tree. Without the argument the read fetches nothing.
alternatives.reason: One plain requested fetch has this Git-owned footprint; it is not an unrecorded tree capture. Architect point3 explicitly accepts the existing test allowance and unchanged command.

alternatives.option: Retain remote-tracking refs and objects only, no tag.
alternatives.reason: The original wording understated what plain git fetch itself writes and was expressly replaced by the later ruling.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A separately admitted fetch command and contract intentionally narrow the ordinary Git footprint.

consequences: Baseline-adoption previews suppress report/snapshot and unfiled pointers; mutating adoption remains a producer.
General read-boundary prose carries(a)-(d), with no unasked fetch and no local branch/HEAD/index/working-tree mutation.
No --no-tags change, new runtime proof, envelope/replay criterion, observer feature or blanket preservation acceptance is inferred.
